transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Wednesday, September 16. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Meta agrees to report child-safety matters directly to Indian authorities. Until Now, It Routed Such Reports Through US Samson's blitz against Afg keeps Sooryavanshi waiting - and the debate alive. Sanju Samson's explosive 57 off 22 balls against Afghanistan in the second T20I was more than a match-winning cameo , it was a compelling reminder of why India's T20I selection calls remain so difficult. Having lost ground to teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Samson responded with fearless batting while acknowledging the challenge of balancing merit, opportunity and India's long-term vision at the top. 'Should be laughed out': T Mobile CFO on Musk's 'Starlink plan' for mobile industry. T-Mobile's CFO Peter Osvaldik stated Starlink Mobile is not a serious wireless threat. He criticized SpaceX's changing strategy and proposed infrastructure plans. Satellites face physical limitations in urban environments, blocking signals. SpaceX's plan for numerous small cell stations is deemed impractical by T-Mobile. 'India, China must be sensitive to each other's concerns': Government on what PM Modi told Xi. PM Narendra Modi raised Indian concerns in ties with China with President Xi Jinping when the two met last week on the sidelines of the Brics summit, saying both sides need to show sensitivity to each other's core concerns, according to the Indian government. Jasprit Bumrah does it again! India star breaks major T20I record against Afg. Jasprit Bumrah opened the bowling for India with a maiden over. It was his 13th maiden in T20I cricket and helped him become the bowler with the most maiden overs among players from Full Member nations. He moved past Zimbabwe's Richard Ngarava, who has bowled 12 maiden overs in T20Is. Free to fee: 0.4 percent on UPI payments over rupees 2,000. National Payments Corporation of India on Tuesday announced a 0.4 percent merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI transactions above rupees 2,000, with an overall cap of rupees 300, and a flat rupees 5 charge for utility payments, fuel purchase, insurance premium, rail tickets, and a host of government services. Airbnb commits $250M to build stalled US housing, starting with Austin. Airbnb has announced a robust initiative to inject $250 million into stalled housing projects, targeting funding shortfalls in construction-ready developments. The first investment of $6.4 million is earmarked for creating affordable housing in Austin, Texas. Additionally, a $5 million innovation prize will encourage advancements in housing technology, all part of Airbnb's commitment to tackling the persistent housing crisis in the United States. After meeting PM Modi, schoolmate gets land back from BJP MLA. Days after an 81-year-old Mira Road resident met his schoolmate, PM Narendra Modi, alleging encroachment of his land in Bhayander by a construction firm owned by BJP MLA Narendra Mehta, the politician said on Tuesday that he is giving up possession of the disputed land and surrendering the nod for construction granted to him for the plot. San Diego mom's extra lasagna for neighbors turns into 750K meals shared. Supermodel Gisele Bündchen has recently made headlines with her acquisition of a stunning 7.5-acre equestrian estate for $9.1 million. This property boasts ten horse stalls and a full-sized soccer field, making it an ideal haven for both sports and equestrian pursuits. With this addition, her Florida real estate portfolio expands further, offering a peaceful retreat that beautifully complements her existing waterfront homes. Egyptian Mummy left 'screaming' for 3,000 years. A remarkable discovery in Thebes reveals an ancient Egyptian mummy with a haunting, frozen scream. Researchers employing cutting-edge technology examined this 3,000-year-old remains and struggled to identify the woman's cause of death. Experts theorize that a sudden occurrence led to cadaveric spasm, preserving her expression, hinting at a tragic demise in great suffering. Work out for 2 months, get Gucci: Indian woman reveals Korean office perk. A fascinating wellness program in South Korea has emerged, where employees are rewarded with luxury fashion gifts for maintaining consistent exercise routines for two months. This initiative aims to foster healthier habits while stimulating conversations about workplace culture and employee support in India. It underlines an increasing awareness of the importance of health-centered benefits in enhancing the workplace experience. Hear us first if Tata Sons files any plea: RBI caveat in HC. Anticipating a legal showdown with Tata Sons, Reserve Bank of India has lodged a caveat in Bombay high court after rejecting its application for deregistration as a core investment company, a status that would have exempted it from a stock market listing.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPI) pulled nearly rupees 5,109.21 crore in the last three days from government securities under the fully accessible route amid dampened sentiments due to global uncertainty.
